input: Find a pediatrician for the new baby

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether the baby is already born or due soon changes the urgency and timeline of the search — many parents need a pediatrician lined up before the birth.
Insurance coverage is a hard limit that filters which pediatricians are actually available; without knowing the plan, any list of candidates could be useless.
The geographic area or proximity requirement directly determines which practices are even worth considering.
If there are specific health needs or conditions for the baby (e.g., prematurity, known diagnosis), that narrows the type of specialist or practice required.
Parents often have strong preferences around care philosophy (e.g., vaccine schedule flexibility, holistic approach, solo vs. group practice) that act as a primary filter.
Knowing what 'done' looks like — a shortlist of names, a confirmed appointment, or a signed-on pediatrician — defines how far the plan needs to go.
Whether the user wants help with the full search process (research, vetting, interviewing) or just a specific step like finding in-network names changes the plan entirely.

gold.taskTitle: Find a pediatrician for the new baby
gold.taskDescription: Research and select a pediatrician for a new baby, covering the full process from identifying candidates to booking a first appointment.

questions.title: When is your baby due or already born?
questions.description: Determine the baby's arrival status to set the urgency and timeline for the search.

questions.title: Which health insurance plan does your baby have?
questions.description: Identify the insurance plan so the search can be filtered to in-network providers only.

questions.title: What city, neighborhood, or max distance are you searching in?
questions.description: Establish the geographic boundaries to make the candidate list practical and usable.

questions.title: Does your baby have any special health needs or conditions?
questions.description: Understand any medical specifics that would require a particular type of practice or specialist experience.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred care philosophy or practice style?
questions.description: Capture preferences such as approach to vaccines, solo vs. group practice, or integrative care to filter candidates meaningfully.

questions.title: What does success look like — a shortlist, or a booked appointment?
questions.description: Define the end goal so the plan covers exactly the right number of steps.

questions.title: Do you want help with the full search or one specific step?
questions.description: Clarify the scope — whether the user needs end-to-end guidance or help with just one part, like finding names or preparing interview questions.
